common_name: Gold Charm Christmas Cactus (Yellow-Flowered Holiday Cactus)

planting.note: Root 2-3 segment stem tip cuttings in well-drained cactus mix or perlite; Gold Charm needs bright indirect light indoors and benefits from a summer vacation outdoors in a shaded location. To induce blooming, expose to cool temperatures (50-55°F) and 12-14 hours of darkness for 4-6 weeks in fall.

directions: Grow in bright indirect light in a well-drained, humus-rich, slightly acidic potting mix, letting the top of the mix dry between waterings. Gold Charm is a holiday cactus cultivar bearing an unusually warm-toned flower color for the group, in soft apricot-gold to peachy yellow rather than the pink, red, or white of most Schlumbergera cultivars, blooming on the same flattened, scalloped-edge stem segments typical of the genus. Like other Christmas cacti it needs a period of cool nights and long uninterrupted darkness in fall to trigger flower bud formation, so avoid exposing it to artificial light at night during that window. Give it a bright but not sun-scorched spot indoors and a shaded outdoor rest each summer for the strongest bloom the following winter.

common_name: Christmas Flame Christmas Cactus (Orange-Red Holiday Cactus)

planting.note: Root 2-3 segment stem tip cuttings in well-drained cactus mix or perlite; Christmas Flame needs bright indirect light indoors and benefits from a summer vacation outdoors in a shaded location. To induce blooming, expose to cool temperatures (50-55°F) and 12-14 hours of darkness for 4-6 weeks in fall.

directions: Grow in bright indirect light in a well-drained, humus-rich, slightly acidic potting mix, letting the top of the mix dry between waterings. Christmas Flame produces vivid orange-red flowers with a hot, fiery tone deeper and warmer than the classic magenta-pink holiday cactus, blooming from the notched, flattened stem segments typical of the genus. It needs the same period of cool nights and long uninterrupted darkness in fall to trigger flower bud formation as other Schlumbergera cultivars, so avoid night-time artificial light during that window. Give it a bright but not sun-scorched spot indoors and a shaded outdoor rest each summer to build strength for the next bloom cycle.

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright indirect light in fast-draining, sandy or cactus-type potting mix; Futura's shorter, broader leaves make it well suited to a small pot or tabletop planting.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright indirect light in fast-draining, sandy or cactus-type potting mix. Futura is a compact snake plant selection with shorter, noticeably wider leaves than the standard trifasciata form, giving each upright fan a stockier, more substantial look in a smaller overall footprint, with the same dark green horizontal banding and pale margin as classic snake plant. Its manageable size fits smaller pots, desks, and shelves better than tall standard forms while still offering the same tolerance for low light and irregular watering. Water only when the soil has dried out completely, since overwatering is by far the most common cause of rot, and divide congested clumps to propagate or refresh an overcrowded pot.

common_name: Boncel Snake Plant (Dwarf Twisted Cylindrical Sansevieria)

planting.note: Divide rooted offsets from the base and pot in fast-draining succulent or cactus mix; grow outdoors in shade to partial sun in zone 10-11 or as a slow-growing indoor houseplant.

directions: Pot in a fast-draining cactus mix and set in bright indirect light to partial sun. Boncel is a dwarf, slow-growing selection of cylindrical snake plant with thick, rounded, banded green leaves fanning out from a compact base, often trained or sold with the leaves loosely braided or twisted together for an even more sculptural, novelty presentation. Its small scale and architectural form make it a popular choice for desks, shelves, and small dish gardens where the full-sized cylindrical snake plant would be too large. It is exceptionally drought-tolerant, needing water only once the potting mix has dried out completely, and largely shrugs off the low humidity and inconsistent light of typical indoor spaces. Avoid overwatering above all else, since soggy soil is the most common cause of rot.

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright indirect light in fast-draining, sandy or cactus-type potting mix; Twist's naturally spiraled leaves make it a distinctive small-pot accent.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright indirect light in fast-draining, sandy or cactus-type potting mix. Twist carries the classic dark green, horizontally banded leaves of standard snake plant, but each leaf spirals and curls as it grows rather than standing flat and straight, giving the whole rosette a lively, corkscrewing form that reads as a novelty accent even in a small pot. Like other snake plants it stores water in thick, succulent leaves and tolerates long stretches of neglect and low light, making it one of the most forgiving houseplants for offices and low-light interiors. Water only when the soil is fully dry, and divide congested clumps to propagate or refresh an overcrowded pot.

planting.note: Divide rooted offsets from the base and pot in fast-draining succulent or cactus mix; grow outdoors in partial shade to full sun in zone 10-11 or as a durable, low-light-tolerant indoor houseplant.

directions: Pot in a fast-draining cactus mix and set in bright indirect light to partial sun outdoors, or in a bright indoor spot. Robusta is a sturdy Indian species with broad, thick, flat, grey-green leaves marked with faint darker mottling, growing in a wide fan from a spreading rhizome and tolerating heat and full outdoor sun better than many other sansevieria species once acclimated. It is exceptionally drought-tolerant, storing water in its thick leaves and needing watering only once the potting mix has dried out completely. Offsets form steadily along the spreading rhizome and can be divided to start new plants once established. Avoid overwatering above all else, since soggy soil is the most common cause of rot.

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded xeriscape container in bright, indirect light in fast-draining, gritty succulent mix; Star Window Plant wants excellent drainage above all else and rots quickly if the soil stays damp.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded xeriscape container in bright, indirect light in fast-draining, gritty succulent mix. Haworthia retusa forms a low, star-shaped rosette of thick, translucent-tipped, blue-green leaves angled sharply upward, each tip forming a small, semi-transparent window that admits light to the leaf interior, a trait shared with its relative Horse's Teeth but in a more open, star-like rosette rather than a tightly clustered fan. It is a slow-growing, long-lived succulent well suited to a small pot, dish garden, or windowsill collection alongside other haworthias. In its native South Africa it grows partly buried in sandy soil with only the leaf tips exposed to filtered light; a similarly gritty, fast-draining mix and bright but indirect light indoors mimics these conditions and helps prevent the rot that comes from overwatering.
